title: Can Fine-Tuning Erase Edits? On the Fragile Coexistence of Knowledge Editing and Fine-tuning

problem.claim: The study examines whether knowledge edits survive subsequent fine-tuning of an edited language model.

gap.claim: Knowledge editing and fine-tuning have been studied in isolation, leaving their interaction insufficiently examined.

contributions.claim: The study systematically quantifies edit decay after fine-tuning across 254 experimental configurations.
Fine-tuning generally causes substantial decay of previously applied edits.
The study analyzes activation-space changes and reports that fine-tuning produces a larger and more coherent representational shift than knowledge editing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: For AlphaEdit on zsRE with GPT-J, 25.27% of previously successful edits became unsuccessful after fine-tuning.
Fine-tuning only edited layers was sufficient to effectively remove edits while causing modest downstream-performance degradation.
Fine-tuning non-edited layers caused greater edit decay than fine-tuning all layers.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge editing provides a lightweight alternative to retraining, while fine-tuning is commonly used for domain and task adaptation.
The interaction between knowledge editing and subsequent fine-tuning has been understudied, raising the question of whether edits survive.
Edit persistence matters for removing covert or malicious edits and preserving beneficial edits, because either outcome creates practical or safety implications.
The study quantifies edit decay after fine-tuning across 254 experimental configurations and examines activation-space changes.
Edits generally decay substantially, with reported differences across edited-layer and all-layer fine-tuning conditions.

source_observation.claim: Fine-tuning generally causes substantial decay of knowledge edits, and fine-tuning non-edited layers can cause greater decay than fine-tuning all layers.

interpretation.claim: The effect of fine-tuning on an edited model may depend on which layers are updated and may not be localized to the edited layers.

application.claim: Systems that combine knowledge editing with later fine-tuning should evaluate edit persistence across layer-selection strategies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the reported decay pattern holds for every editing method, model, benchmark, or fine-tuning setup.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the full set of models, editing methods, benchmarks, or fine-tuning configurations.
The abstract does not provide detailed evaluation protocols or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported findings.
